scenarios.hypothesis: A serialized discriminator that passes syntax and schema validation must not authorize construction until resolver identity, registry generation, and canonical runtime type identity match the approved reconstruction policy.
scenarios.safe_oracle: Use a controlled local decoder with a mock type registry, synthetic discriminator values, inert fixture classes, and a read-only canary receipt so no external capability is touched.
scenarios.positive_control: An approved synthetic discriminator under the current schema and registry generation resolves to the intended inert data class and returns the expected read-only synthetic receipt.
scenarios.negative_control: Keep parser bytes and schema validity constant while a neighboring synthetic alias resolves to a non-approved inert type; policy must reject the canonical identity before construction.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if validation would require a production object graph, command execution, file modification, external network access, real secrets, persistence, destructive behavior, or any unauthorized target.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After remediation, policy evaluates the canonical resolved runtime identity and rejects the previously accepted alias while the intended current-generation synthetic data type still reconstructs successfully.
scenarios.artifact_origin: The artifact is generated by a deterministic local fixture representing a lower-authority synthetic sender and carries a unique test identity rather than production user or service data.
scenarios.envelope_authentication_context: The fixture envelope is signed by a synthetic principal whose authority is limited to ordinary data submission, keeping authenticity scope explicitly separate from runtime type-selection authority.
scenarios.format_parser_identity: One pinned local serializer/parser implementation and configuration processes all paired controls so parser-version or format differences cannot explain the registry-resolution outcome.
scenarios.canonical_field_state: The parser produces a deterministic canonical field map with identical ordinary data across controls and one normalized discriminator captured before schema and resolver decisions occur.
scenarios.schema_identity_version: A pinned synthetic schema identity and version permits the discriminator field structurally while delegating runtime-type authorization to the explicit reconstruction policy being reviewed.
scenarios.discriminator_state: The control pair changes only the approved versus neighboring synthetic alias while recording both serialized selector and normalized selector before registry lookup.
scenarios.registry_resolver_identity: A mock resolver with a stable fixture identity owns an explicit alias-to-canonical-type table, independent from attacker-controlled namespace, package, or selector spelling.
scenarios.registry_generation: A concrete monotonic registry generation is captured in every resolution and policy decision so stale aliases or prior mappings cannot silently inherit current reconstruction authority.
scenarios.runtime_type_identity: Each selector resolves to a canonical inert runtime type identity, and authorization is evaluated on that identity rather than textual alias, prefix, namespace, or registry-key spelling.
scenarios.object_construction_path: The approved path constructs an inert data-only fixture through a deterministic factory; the non-approved canonical type must be denied before allocation or behavior-bearing initialization.
scenarios.hook_callback_surface: Fixture classes have no harmful behavior; a synthetic marker hook only records whether construction was entered by appending to a controlled in-memory event ledger.
scenarios.secondary_interpretation: Ordinary fields are not interpreted as paths, templates, expressions, queries, policies, or plugins in this case, isolating canonical type resolution as the tested security transition.
scenarios.authority_context: The synthetic sender may submit schema-conforming data but is not authorized to choose arbitrary runtime classes, making represented data authority intentionally narrower than resolver capability.
scenarios.requested_reconstructed_capability: The positive request asks only for the approved inert data class while the negative alias requests a neighboring canonical runtime identity outside the sender's permitted reconstruction set.
scenarios.policy_decision: The reconstruction policy binds normalized selector, schema identity/version, resolver identity, registry generation, and canonical runtime type into a deterministic allow-or-deny decision.
scenarios.effective_reconstructed_authority: Allowed authority is limited to creation of the approved inert data object with no filesystem, process, device, credential, plugin, or external network capability.
scenarios.privileged_consumer: The consumer is a mock local object receiver that can inspect inert fixture data and emit a deterministic canary receipt but cannot invoke real privileged services or resources.
scenarios.bounded_result: The valid path returns a read-only synthetic canary naming the canonical type; the rejected alias returns explicit denial and produces no construction marker or external effect.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Every canary or denial binds artifact identity, schema version, normalized selector, resolver identity, registry generation, canonical runtime type, and policy-decision identifier.
scenarios.lifecycle_generation: A paired control advances the mock registry generation while other inputs remain stable to prove prior alias mappings do not inherit current authority by logical-name reuse.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Replay the same canonical field map first with a neighboring alias and then under a changed registry generation while holding all unrelated fields constant to isolate the resolution transition.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Exclude parser fallback, default-type insertion, schema migration, accidental fixture registration, alias collision, registry reload race, stale marker state, and receipt correlation with another synthetic request.
scenarios.evidence_level: Target evidence is DT5 only when wrong canonical type acceptance reaches a bounded inert result and the complete selector-to-resolver-to-policy chain plus remediation is proven causally.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: Without a bounded causally bound result and exact canonical runtime type plus registry-generation proof, the evidence ceiling stays below DT4 even if textual alias acceptance is observed.

scenarios.hypothesis: A syntactically valid or correctly authenticated object must not acquire constructor, post-load, callback, plugin, or secondary-interpreter behavior broader than the initiating principal's approved reconstructed authority.
scenarios.safe_oracle: Use a synthetic authenticated sender, inert callback marker, mock plugin consumer, and controlled in-memory event ledger; the oracle observes only benign marker state and never performs a real command, write, or network action.
scenarios.positive_control: The approved synthetic data-only object reconstructs with ordinary fields and no behavior marker, or invokes only the explicitly permitted inert callback when policy grants that exact capability.
scenarios.negative_control: Keep envelope authentication, parser, schema, and runtime type unchanged while requesting a neighboring inert hook capability outside sender scope; policy must deny it before behavior executes.
scenarios.stop_condition: Abort and do not proceed if proof would require command execution, arbitrary file modification, outbound network access, production credentials, persistence, malware, destructive behavior, or any system outside explicit authorization.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After remediation, the over-broad synthetic hook or secondary interpretation is blocked while intended data-only reconstruction and explicitly allowed inert neighboring behavior continue unchanged.
scenarios.artifact_origin: The serialized artifact is created by a deterministic synthetic principal modeled as authorized to submit configuration data but not to select behavior-bearing callbacks, plugins, resource openers, or privileged interpreters.
scenarios.envelope_authentication_context: A mock signature validates synthetic sender identity and data-submission purpose, deliberately demonstrating that valid authenticity is narrower than authority to select arbitrary reconstructed behavior.
scenarios.format_parser_identity: One pinned parser configuration processes positive and negative artifacts identically through syntax decoding so a later marker difference cannot be attributed to parser drift.
scenarios.canonical_field_state: A stable canonical field map keeps ordinary values equal across controls while one synthetic capability selector requests either data-only behavior or a neighboring inert callback/plugin marker.
scenarios.schema_identity_version: A fixed synthetic schema version accepts the capability-selector field structurally, exposing the separate reconstruction-policy decision instead of hiding the hypothesis behind schema rejection.
scenarios.discriminator_state: The discriminator resolves to the same approved inert runtime type for both controls; only a behavior-bearing callback or plugin selector changes after type resolution.
scenarios.registry_resolver_identity: A mock type resolver always selects the same canonical fixture class while a separate controlled callback/plugin registry resolves the requested behavior identity under a pinned generation.
scenarios.registry_generation: Both type-registry and callback/plugin-registry generations are recorded so an inert marker cannot be attributed to stale resolver state or an earlier policy generation.
scenarios.runtime_type_identity: Both controls reconstruct the same canonical inert runtime type identity, preventing unexpected class selection from being confused with hook-capability authorization.
scenarios.object_construction_path: Construction follows the same deterministic factory and property-binding sequence for both controls, with behavior activation deferred until policy evaluates the explicit synthetic capability request.
scenarios.hook_callback_surface: The only behavior-bearing surface is an inert callback or mock plugin that appends a canary token to controlled memory and has no interface to real privileged functionality.
scenarios.secondary_interpretation: A controlled string becomes a callback/plugin key only after ordinary schema validation, and the trace records that semantic transition separately from the original data representation.
scenarios.authority_context: The synthetic principal owns the ordinary data values but its authenticated purpose excludes arbitrary behavior selection, keeping data ownership distinct from reconstructed-behavior authority.
scenarios.requested_reconstructed_capability: The negative fixture requests one named inert callback/plugin capability outside the principal's approved data-only scope while the positive control remains within the authorized purpose.
scenarios.policy_decision: Policy combines authenticated sender scope, schema identity, canonical runtime type, requested inert behavior identity, registry generation, and consumer context before activation.
scenarios.effective_reconstructed_authority: The positive path receives only data-object authority or one explicitly permitted inert marker; the negative path must not inherit the consumer's broader ambient callback/plugin capability.
scenarios.privileged_consumer: A mock reconstruction consumer owns the inert callback/plugin registry and emits deterministic receipts but has no filesystem, process, credential, device, or external network interface.
scenarios.bounded_result: Authorized reconstruction yields a synthetic data receipt, while an improperly authorized hook can yield only an in-memory canary marker; no harmful side effect is necessary for proof.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Each receipt or marker event binds artifact ID, synthetic principal, requested behavior identity, canonical runtime type, policy decision, registry generation, and unique fixture correlation ID.
scenarios.lifecycle_generation: A paired control advances callback/plugin policy generation and verifies a previously permitted synthetic behavior does not survive revocation through cached or restored reconstructed state.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold authenticated sender, parser, schema, and runtime type constant while changing only requested inert behavior, then hold behavior constant while narrowing sender purpose/scope.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Exclude expected post-load behavior, accidental marker initialization, callback registry collision, stale ledger entries, schema-default behavior, debug-only permissiveness, and correlation with another fixture run.
scenarios.evidence_level: DT5 requires a causally bound inert marker or bounded receipt plus complete authenticity, type, hook, authority, policy, lifecycle, counterfactual, alternative-explanation, and remediation evidence.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: Hook reachability, valid authentication, or callback names without a bounded causally correlated result remain below DT4; arbitrary-code or system-compromise claims exceed this evidence.

scenarios.hypothesis: Schema, registry, policy, plugin, or persisted-object generation changes must invalidate stale reconstruction authority instead of letting an old artifact inherit current type mappings or capabilities by logical-name reuse.
scenarios.safe_oracle: Use controlled old/current schema and registry generations, synthetic persisted artifacts, a mock resolver, and an inert read-only canary consumer so lifecycle behavior is observed without production data or external effects.
scenarios.positive_control: A current-generation synthetic artifact using current schema, registry mapping, and policy reconstructs the intended inert data object and produces a fresh correctly bound read-only canary receipt.
scenarios.negative_control: Replay an otherwise identical stale synthetic artifact after registry or policy generation advances; stale state must be rejected rather than inheriting the current mapping or reconstructed capability.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop if testing stale reconstruction would require retaining real secrets, production sessions, unauthorized persisted state, arbitrary execution, external network interaction, destructive mutation, persistence, or third-party systems.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After generation-aware remediation, stale synthetic artifacts and resolver bindings are rejected while a freshly encoded current-generation artifact preserves intended data-only reconstruction behavior.
scenarios.artifact_origin: The fixture creates deterministic serialized state before a controlled schema/registry transition and labels it with a synthetic origin and generation so no production session or user-owned artifact is required.
scenarios.envelope_authentication_context: Stale and current artifacts use the same mock authenticated principal, allowing the test to isolate lifecycle invalidation rather than sender-authentication differences.
scenarios.format_parser_identity: The same pinned parser implementation processes old and current controls, with any explicit migration step recorded separately so parser replacement cannot explain stale-authority acceptance.
scenarios.canonical_field_state: Old and current artifacts normalize into comparable deterministic field maps with a recorded generation-bearing selector or metadata difference tied to the controlled lifecycle transition.
scenarios.schema_identity_version: Old and current synthetic schema versions plus migration policy are recorded; logical schema-name reuse cannot erase the authoritative generation associated with reconstruction authority.
scenarios.discriminator_state: The human-readable discriminator may remain stable across the transition, demonstrating that identical selector text can resolve under different authoritative registry generations.
scenarios.registry_resolver_identity: One mock resolver identity owns a table intentionally updated between generations, making the mapping transition explicit and deterministic rather than dependent on external plugin discovery.
scenarios.registry_generation: Monotonic old and current registry generations are included in policy and receipt records; stale mappings cannot be accepted merely because alias or class label text is unchanged.
scenarios.runtime_type_identity: The canonical runtime type selected before and after the controlled transition is recorded, including a fixture where one logical alias maps to a neighboring inert type in the new generation.
scenarios.object_construction_path: Current artifacts use the current deterministic factory path, while stale artifacts must be rejected before construction when authoritative schema/registry/policy generation no longer matches.
scenarios.hook_callback_surface: Any fixture hook is an inert in-memory marker used only to detect whether stale construction crossed the behavior boundary and cannot invoke command, file, network, or credential capabilities.
scenarios.secondary_interpretation: If a persisted field later becomes a mock plugin or policy key, interpreter generation is captured and current binding is required rather than silently reusing stale semantic meaning.
scenarios.authority_context: The synthetic principal remains constant while allowed reconstruction context advances to the current policy generation, isolating stale lifecycle state from ordinary principal-membership changes.
scenarios.requested_reconstructed_capability: Stale and current artifacts request the same benign data-only or read-only canary capability so generation validity is the only intended security-relevant difference.
scenarios.policy_decision: Current policy binds artifact generation, schema version, registry generation, canonical runtime type, principal scope, and requested capability before any reconstructed object reaches the consumer.
scenarios.effective_reconstructed_authority: Only a current-generation artifact receives narrow data-only or read-only canary authority; stale artifacts receive no reconstructed capability even when logical names remain valid.
scenarios.privileged_consumer: The consumer is a mock local state restorer that can return only an inert canary receipt for approved current-generation objects and cannot access real privileged system resources.
scenarios.bounded_result: The current artifact returns a deterministic read-only synthetic canary while stale artifacts return explicit generation denial and create no construction marker, callback event, or external side effect.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Each result binds artifact identity, synthetic principal, schema version, registry generation, policy generation, canonical runtime type, requested capability, and unique fixture correlation ID.
scenarios.lifecycle_generation: Schema, registry, or policy generation advances through a documented deterministic transition while both old and current fixture identities are preserved for exact stale/current comparison.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Replay with only old registry generation, then only old schema generation, then only old policy generation while parser, principal, capability, and ordinary data remain constant.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Exclude migration bugs unrelated to authority, parser fallback, resolver reload races, stale cache telemetry, duplicate fixture IDs, alias collisions, benign retries, and receipts from previous runs.
scenarios.evidence_level: DT5 requires the bounded canary plus exact old/current generation provenance, canonical type and policy traces, independent lifecycle counterfactuals, alternative elimination, and remediation regression.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: Logical-name reuse or observation of stale bytes without a causally bound accepted result remains below DT4; DT5 requires proving stale reconstructed authority across the exact lifecycle chain.
